policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 3:2 is only 'Repent ye; for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.' The connective joining the preaching participle to 'saying' is not rendered by any English word here, so neither the presence nor the absence of kai is visible.
ASV reads 'spoken of through Isaiah the prophet': 'through' renders dia, whereas hypo would give the agentive 'by'. The English preposition distinguishes the base reading.

The candidates differ only in the order of en autou; ASV 'Now John himself had his raiment of camel's hair' fixes English word order independently of the Greek sequence, so no wording distinguishes them.
ASV reads 'in the river Jordan'; the noun 'river' renders potamo, which the omitting reading lacks.

ASV reads 'coming to his baptism'; the possessive 'his' renders autou, absent from the omitting reading. The 'Or, for baptism' note is an alternative_rendering about the preposition and does not bear on the pronoun.

ASV 'And even now the axe lieth at the root' can render ede de alone, 'even now' being ordinary English for ede, as readily as ede de kai. The adverb is not a reliable trace of an added kai, so the English does not settle it.

The candidates differ only in the order of hymas baptizo; ASV 'I indeed baptize you in water' renders both identically. The two notes here are alternative_rendering ('Or, with') and a Greek gloss, neither of which touches word order.
ASV reads 'in the Holy Spirit and in fire'; 'and in fire' renders kai pyri, which the omitting reading lacks.
ASV reads 'gather his wheat into the garner' — the possessive attaches to the wheat (autou with siton), and the garner is left unmodified, so the added autou after apotheken is not rendered.
ASV names the subject: 'But John would have hindered him'. The proper name renders Ioannes, which the omitting reading lacks.

ASV 'said unto him' renders pros auton and the simple dative auto alike; English has no way to distinguish the prepositional phrase from the dative. The 'Or, me' note is an alternative_rendering elsewhere in the verse.
ASV opens 'And Jesus, when he was baptized', which suits baptistheis de and Kai baptistheis equally; the English conjunction 'And' is compatible with either de or kai.
The candidates differ only in the order of euthys and anebe; ASV 'went up straightway from the water' places the adverb by English idiom and does not reflect the Greek sequence.

ASV reads 'the heavens were opened unto him', and the mapped textual_variant note 'Some ancient authorities omit unto him' confirms auto stands in the ASV text; this excludes the base reading without auto. The remaining two readings differ only in the augment of the verb (eneochthesan vs aneochthesan), which English cannot show.

ASV 'the Spirit of God' is the normal English for both the anarthrous pneuma theou and the articular to pneuma tou theou; English supplies 'the' either way, so the articles do not distinguish the readings.
ASV reads 'descending as a dove, and coming upon him'; the coordinating 'and' before the second participle renders the kai that the base reading lacks.
